absent: No committed test or receipt pins the base/head field identity; the identity is demonstrated only by the run's scratch comparator (deleted) and by this review's independent differential.
No batched (vmap) H200 wall is recorded, so the H200 arm does not demonstrate the throughput regime in which the card is expected to beat CPU.

absent_items.why: the comparator establishing field-by-field base/head identity ran from /tmp and was not committed; only its {nodes, edges, overflow} summary survives in the repository.

absent_items.item: durable perf regression bound in the committed gate
absent_items.why: the only wall-clock assertion lives in a scratch negative-control test; the committed 33-test gate carries no performance bound.

findings.text: follow-on: check 1 holds and was strengthened independently: the run claims the base/head receipt comparison covers every field on all 18 fixtures, but the committed comparator logs (docs/figures/contour-tree-topology-authority/sweep-cost/base-head-receipt-comparison.log) print only {nodes, edges, overflow} per fixture and the comparator itself (/tmp/ctta_receipt_compare_chunk.py) is uncommitted and gone, so 'every field' is not verifiable from the committed artifact. I rebuilt both trees (base 11985735c via git archive, head 73d557eb6 from the reviewed worktree) and compared every ContourTreeArrays field (node_vertex, node_psi, node_valid, critical_type, edges, edge_valid, overflow) on 13 certificate fixtures plus 35 synthetic graphs (grids, a degree-11 star, and 40 random graphs carrying self-loops, duplicate edges, invalid vertices and wall masks): 48 cases, 336 fields, 0 mismatches (run dir review-evidence/base-head-all-field-differential.log). The identity claim is therefore true, but the run's own committed evidence under-states its coverage. The 3 rung fixtures and 2 MAST fixtures in the run's 18 were not independently re-run on the base arm: the base fixture sweep exceeded a 10-minute budget (base is 200x slower on the largest rung), so those five rest on the run's own summary comparator; the all-field identity is established independently on the other 13 plus 35 synthetic graphs.

follow-on: check 2: the replacement of the segmented max with a duplicate-index scatter is equivalent, by an argument the differential tests but no committed test names. parents.at[neighbour_root].set(where(root_active & usable, vertex, parents[neighbour_root])) is safe because two neighbour slots that share a root are in the same union-find component and are therefore always both active, so every duplicate write of that root carries the same value vertex; the random-graph arm above (cycles produce duplicate roots) confirms no observable difference from the base build.

follow-on: check 3: complexity stated from the code. _carrier_adjacency indexes each edge once into an O(V*C) table with C = min(edge_count, 16); the per-visit repeated check is O(C^2) over the 16-wide neighbour row instead of O(E^2) over the full edge buffer, so the bounded-degree carrier sweep falls from base O(V*(V+E) + V*E^2) to about O(V + E). I reproduced BOTH arms on the 1074-cell fixture (1089 vertices, 3478 edges): base 96.995 s vs head 0.464 s, about 209x, against the run's recorded 100.381 s -> 0.490 s.

follow-on: check 4, H200 vs CPU: at 1089 vertices the H200 execute is 2.772 s against 0.490 s on CPU, so CPU is about 5.7x faster for a single field. This is the expected shape of a sequential sweep: _sweep_tree is a jax.lax.fori_loop of V visits run twice, each running a data-dependent jax.lax.while_loop, so the device is launch-latency bound and the card is under-used. The H200 lane therefore wins on throughput under batching, not single-field latency; I confirmed build_contour_tree is traceable and fixed-shape under jax.vmap (batched node_vertex (4,256), edges (4,255,2), identical per-field to a loop of jitted single calls), but no vmap-batched H200 wall was measured, so the marked H200 arm is a correctness/latency receipt rather than a demonstrated throughput win.

follow-on: the two capacity tests raise a JAX FutureWarning, 'scatter inputs have incompatible types: cannot safely cast value from dtype=int64 to dtype=int32 with jax_numpy_dtype_promotion=standard. In future JAX releases this will result in an error', from the new int64 index/scatter in _carrier_adjacency (test_carrier_neighbour_capacity_overflow_is_visible and test_critical_node_capacity_overflow_is_jittable_and_visible, head-topology-gate.log warnings summary). Pin the index dtype so a JAX upgrade does not turn the refusal tests into errors.

follow-on: check 5, negative control fires: restoring the base repeated-neighbour matrix makes test_sweep_execute_bound fail at 101.056 s against its 2.0 s bound, EXIT=1, single failing id test_sweep_execute_bound (line 20). The guard the change adds is a wall-clock assertion in a scratch test (/tmp/sweep_negative_control.py, now gone), so it is non-deterministic by construction; the committed 33-test gate does not carry a perf bound, and the sought proof of the perf change is the measured scaling rather than a durable test.

justifications.durability: The change, its overflow regression test, the figure and the H200 log are committed to the reviewed branch and the worktree is clean, but two load-bearing instruments are uncommitted scratch: the field comparator that supports the identity claim and the negative-control perf test, so neither is reproducible from the repository after the run's /tmp scratch is reaped.
justifications.evidence: The measurements are strong and independently reproduced (CPU 0.464 s; 48-case all-field differential 336 fields 0 mismatches; negative control EXIT=1), but the run's own committed evidence for its central identity claim is a 3-scalar-per-fixture summary whose comparator is uncommitted and deleted, and the perf guard is a non-deterministic scratch timing test.
justifications.fit: The new symbols _carrier_adjacency and _neighbour_roots are mechanism-named and their docstrings explain the bounded-degree carrier table and the visible capacity refusal; no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in symbols, comments, filenames or the commit subjects and each commit carries a body.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The indexed sweep lands the intended cost reduction and the run's numbers reproduce: the committed CPU rungs fall 6.105 -> 0.084 s, 19.320 -> 0.198 s and 100.381 -> 0.490 s at 353/558/1089 vertices, I re-measured 0.464 s at 1089 vertices, the 33-test topology gate passes (after-topology-suite.log 33 passed), the H200 arm completed with CudaDevice(id=0) and EXIT_STATUS=0, and the receipt identity holds. The H200 single-field arm is slower than CPU (2.772 vs 0.490 s), which is a property of the sequential sweep rather than a goal miss.
justifications.scope_discipline: The four commits b973adbc1, cae331a08, 3ab1adef4 and 73d557eb6 union to eight files, all inside the declared write paths (nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py, tests/test_contour_tree_merge.py, docs/figures/contour-tree-topology-authority/sweep-cost/*, docs/evidence/fragments/contour-tree-topology-authority/ctta-sweep-cost-on-carrier-size.html), and the reviewed worktree is clean.
